item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Esha looks at the figure. Segments $AB$ and $CD$ meet at $M$, and a square mark sits at $\angle AMC$.

Which claim is correct?

options.A: $\angle AMC$ is a right angle, so $AB$ and $CD$ are perpendicular at $M$.
options.B: $AB$ and $CD$ are perpendicular at $M$ for any crossing of the two segments, even without a right angle at $M$.
options.C: Every pair of segments drawn through $M$ must form a straight angle at $M$.
options.D: The answer is "right angle" only because the square mark is the darkest print near $M$.
